name: Northeast Buttress

approach_variants.name: Cathedral Rock Trail to the pass, then a rising traverse under the east face
approach_variants.notes:
From I-90 exit 80 at Cle Elum, take SR-903 north through Roslyn and Ronald along Cle Elum Lake for about 14.8 miles, then gravel Cle Elum Valley Road / FR 4330 for 12.3 miles and the short NF-153 spur to the Cathedral Rock trailhead, Trail #1345, at about 3,350 ft. Sign the free self-issue wilderness permit.

The trail climbs through old growth to Nosh Nosh Wahtum, formerly Squaw Lake, at about 4,850 ft and 2.5 miles, then opens into meadow with Cathedral Rock ahead. At about 4 miles you reach Cathedral Pass at 5,550 ft and the PCT junction.

Walk north on the PCT for a couple of minutes, then cut across the meadow to a stand of trees. Parties cache the gear they do not need on the climb there. From the trees, start a rising traverse under the east face, past the meadows, and then across a loose talus slope with the northeast buttress in sight.

About 6.4 km and 3,400 ft.
approach_variants.season: July to September. The northeast side is shaded and dries slowly, so give it time after rain and expect approach snow into July
hazards: Loose, fractured andesite throughout — poor and unpredictable protection on every technical route on this peak
A short steep snowfield with loose and sharp rock below it, crossed by parties in approach shoes
The moat at the top of the snow
Rockfall down the gully systems from parties, wind and thaw
Descent route-finding on the shattered south and southwest flanks, where many plausible gullies cliff out
Summer convection over the Cascade crest, on an exposed tower with no cell coverage and a remote trailhead
approach_variants.baseFinding:
The route starts at the top of a short, steep snowfield, and that snowfield is the arrival test. Crossing the loose talus under the east face you come to it; it is short but steep enough that parties in approach shoes have picked their way up it holding stones for security. Reaching the top of that snow patch is reaching the start of the climbing.

And here is the mistake parties actually make at that point, which is the most useful thing to know about this route: at the top of the snow it is natural to exit right onto ledges and start up from there. That is wrong. A party that does it finds the ground harder than the fourth class the description promises, wanders left, right and up, and comes back down. The correct start is to exit back left into the moat at the top of the snow, where the terrain is much easier.

So the test is a difficulty test: if your first moves off the snow feel harder than fourth class, you are on the wrong side of the snowfield. Go back and take the moat on the left.

What should follow: easy ground you can simul-climb, then a ledge system that traverses rightward toward the crest of the buttress. Beckey gives the buttress seven pitches, about 900 ft, at 5.7 and grade III. A route that is sustained from the first pitch is not it.

And one thing to settle before you leave the trees: this peak is descended by the south side, not by reversing the buttress. Note where you came up.

itinerary: Long single day: leave the trailhead around 5-6am, at the base of the snowfield by mid-morning, seven pitches through the middle of the day, summit early-to-mid afternoon, descend the south side and hike out — expect 12-14 hours car to car. Two-day version: camp at Nosh Nosh Wahtum or near Cathedral Pass, start the climb early on day two with a light pack, and walk out that afternoon. The published trip report's party left at 6:20am specifically to beat the heat and to have time to crag afterwards, which gives a sense of the pace a competent team can manage.

waypoints.name: Cathedral Rock Trailhead (Trail #1345)
waypoints.directions: Leave I-90 at Exit 80 and follow SR-903 north through Roslyn and Ronald and along Cle Elum Lake for about 14.8 miles to where the maintained road ends, then continue about 12.3 miles on the gravel Cle Elum Valley Road (FR 4330) and the short NF-153 spur to the Cathedral Rock trailhead for Trail #1345, at about 3,350 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park, and a free wilderness permit is self-issued at the trailhead.

waypoints.name: Nosh Nosh Wahtum (formerly Squaw Lake) — water and campsites
waypoints.directions: Take Trail #1345 across the bridge over the Cle Elum River, entering the wilderness at about 0.5 mile, and climb through old growth past the Trail Creek Trail #1332 junction at about 2 miles to Nosh Nosh Wahtum, the lake at about 4,850 ft, 2.5 miles in.

waypoints.name: Cathedral Pass / Pacific Crest Trail junction — leave the trail here for the meadow and gear cache
waypoints.directions: Continue on Trail #1345 as it opens into meadows with Cathedral Rock ahead, climbing to Cathedral Pass and the Pacific Crest Trail junction at 5,550 ft, about 4 miles from the trailhead.

waypoints.name: Cathedral Rock summit
waypoints.directions: Walk north on the PCT for a couple of minutes, then cut across the meadow to a stand of trees where parties cache gear. Make a rising traverse under the east face, past meadows and across loose talus, to a short steep snowfield below the buttress. From its top exit left into the moat, simul-climb easy ground and a ledge system rightward to the crest, and climb about seven pitches (5.7) up the buttress to the summit.
